document.definition: A self-contained tender or contract artifact that stands alone as a deliverable — a top-level Exhibit (e.g. Exhibit A, Exhibit A7, Exhibit M), a named map, report, plan, drawing, or specification that has its own document number or title. DO NOT use for Appendices or numbered sub-sections of an Exhibit (e.g. Appendix A1.3, Appendix A1.4) — those are sections.
examples: Exhibit M – Contractor's Organisation and Key Personnel
Technical Specification for CCS Compressor Package

section.definition: A numbered or named subdivision INSIDE a document — a chapter, clause group, appendix, or sub-exhibit whose locator is tied to its parent (e.g. Appendix A1.3 lives inside Exhibit A1). Use this for anything prefixed Appendix, Schedule, Annex, or Section when it is a sub-part of a larger document. DO NOT use for top-level Exhibits (Exhibit A, Exhibit B, Exhibit A7, etc.) — those are documents.
examples: Appendix A1.3 - ILNG Facility Roads and Other Areas
Appendix A1.4 - Site Installed Plant Envelope Map

clause.definition: A single, atomic contractual provision identified by a clause number — the smallest contractually binding unit of text. It expresses one obligation, requirement, condition, or definition.

test.definition: A defined verification or qualification activity with explicit pass/fail criteria, performed at a specific point in the project lifecycle to demonstrate compliance of equipment, systems, or work.

functional_group.definition: A grouping of equipment or systems by engineering function or discipline — not a single tagged system. Used in EPC scope breakdowns to bundle related systems for design, procurement, or testing purposes.

system.definition: A physical or logical engineered subsystem of the plant or product being delivered — typically identified by a tag, unit number, or named function. The lowest level at which Mechanical Completion and commissioning are tracked. Distinct from individual equipment items: a system is composed of equipment.

equipment.definition: A specific tagged physical item installed in or supplied to the plant — pumps, vessels, valves, motors, instruments, heat exchangers. Identified by an equipment tag number such as P-101 or V-2305. Lower granularity than a system; equipment is what a system is built from.

material.definition: A substance, material grade, coating, or commodity specified for the work — typically referenced by a standard grade or material specification. Refers to the material itself, not equipment fabricated from it.
examples: ASTM A106 Grade B carbon steel

requirement.definition: A technical or contractual requirement statement — a 'shall' statement that defines a property, characteristic, or capability the work must possess. Often quantitative.
examples: MTBF shall be greater than 5000 hours
noise level shall not exceed 85 dB(A) at 1 m

obligation.definition: A legal or contractual duty imposed on a named party — an action verb phrase such as deliver, provide, indemnify, warrant, notify, comply with. Distinct from a technical 'shall' on the work itself.
examples: Vendor shall notify within 14 days of any non-conformance
Bidder shall maintain professional indemnity insurance

condition.definition: A pre-condition or post-condition that must be satisfied for something else to happen — typically expressed with 'subject to', 'provided that', 'after', 'upon completion of', or 'unless'.
examples: upon issuance of the Taking Over Certificate
provided that all close-out reports have been accepted

deliverable.definition: A tangible work product that the Contractor or Vendor must hand over to the Company — documents, drawings, hardware, software, spare parts, training, certificates. Each deliverable has an owner, due date, and acceptance criteria.

penalty.definition: A financial or contractual consequence levied for non-compliance, late performance, or breach — typically liquidated damages, performance LDs, retention forfeiture, or cure-period sanctions. Has a stated calculation rule and often a cap.
examples: Performance LDs for shortfall in capacity
Cap on liability at 100% of contract price

approval.definition: A formal authorisation or sign-off step — a discrete review gate where the Company, Authority, or Engineer must accept a deliverable, design, or activity before work can proceed.

milestone.definition: A named scheduled event or date marker in the project programme — a fixed point used for progress measurement or contractual gates. Distinct from a payment event: a milestone is a project event, even if a payment is linked to it.

payment.definition: A scheduled payment, payment milestone, retention release, or invoiceable financial event in the contract payment schedule — the financial event itself. Distinct from `amount` (the figure) and from `milestone` (the project event the payment may be linked to).

role.definition: A contractual job function or position — the named role itself, not a specific person filling it. Includes Company, Contractor, and third-party functions defined by the contract.

discipline.definition: An engineering or operational discipline used to organise scope, deliverables, or responsibility — Civil, Mechanical, Process, Electrical, Instrumentation & Control, HSE, Piping, Structural. Distinct from a job role (a role is a position; a discipline is a field of work) and distinct from a functional_group (a discipline is the field; a functional_group is a bundle of equipment).

standard.definition: A formal published technical or industry standard referenced as a compliance basis — issued by a recognised standards body such as API, ASME, ISO, IEC, ANSI, NACE, AS/NZS.

regulation.definition: A statutory or legal regulation issued by a government, regulator, or competent authority — has the force of law in a specific jurisdiction. Compliance is not optional.
examples: NT Work Health and Safety Act 2011

permit.definition: A regulatory permit, license, certificate, or authorisation issued by a government body or regulator — required by law before specified work can proceed. Distinct from `approval` (an internal contract gate) and from `regulation` (a permit is the artefact granted under a regulation).

organization.definition: A registered legal entity or recognised institutional body — operator, contractor, sub-contractor, vendor, regulator, certifying body, joint-venture partner. Always a named legal person.

location.definition: A geographic place or fixed facility location — country, state, city, field, plant site, jetty, or named area where work is performed or equipment is installed.

amount.definition: A monetary value with its currency — always extracted as a single string that includes both the number and the currency code or name. Used for contract price, payments, fees, bond values, caps, and any sum of money. Currency on its own is NOT a separate entity; it travels with the value.
examples: Bid Bond of 2% of Contract Price

bond.definition: A financial security instrument required by the contract — bid bond, performance bond, advance payment guarantee, parent company guarantee, retention bond, standby letter of credit. Refers to the instrument itself, not the monetary value of it (the value is an `amount`) and not the obligation to provide it (which is an `obligation`).

insurance.definition: A named insurance policy or coverage type required to be held by Contractor, Vendor, or sub-contractor. Refers to the policy or coverage itself, not the obligation to maintain it (which is an `obligation`) and not the policy limit (which is an `amount`).

duration.definition: A time span or period — a length of time, not a specific date. Used for warranty periods, notice periods, cure periods, response times, defect liability windows.

threshold.definition: A non-monetary numerical limit, boundary, or tolerance with its unit of measure — extracted as a single string that includes both the number and the unit. Covers minimums, maximums, ranges, percentages, and tolerances. Unit on its own is NOT a separate entity; it travels with the value.

term.definition: A defined contractual term whose meaning is fixed by the contract or referenced documents — typically capitalised, listed in a Definitions clause, and used consistently throughout the contract. Extract only when the chunk DEFINES the term, not every time the term is used.

person.definition: A named individual human — a real person identified by full name. Used for signatories, named representatives, point-of-contact persons, or witnesses.

project.definition: The overall named project, programme, or development — the umbrella name under which the contract is executed. Typically branded and singular per ITB.

risk.definition: An identified risk, hazard, or threat captured in a risk register, HAZID, HAZOP, or contractor risk schedule — the named risk event itself, not the consequence or the mitigation. Used for safety, schedule, commercial, and technical risk tracking.
examples: design change after Issued For Construction
